transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-06-09
Time: 10:00 PT
Duration: ~72 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan (CEO); Priya Singh (CTO); Diego Ramos (Head of Product); Samira Patel (VP Eng); Jae Kim (Head of Customer); All employees (virtual)

[00:00] Alex Morgan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, kicking off June all-hands. Quick note, recording is on, and we've got about an hour and change. I'm gonna run through some high-level numbers and then hand to Priya for infra and to Diego for product. Please put questions in the q&a and we'll save 20 minutes at the end.

[00:30] Alex Morgan: Quick highlights — ARR growth is trending well, we closed three new dedicated deals this quarter, two at enterprise scale. Net retention's holding around 113% which is great, churn still low. We hit a pretty big milestone on latency — median p95 for short chats is down about 18% from March after some of the kernel and batching changes. Big props to infra and eng.

[01:10] Priya Singh: Thanks Alex. Hey team. So infra update, we've rolled the new kernel selector into prod last month. There's still some tuning to do; some models saw regressions on long-context cases, so we're iterating. The continuous batching changes plus improved KV cache handling reduced token spend by about 12% in our Hosted fleet. There are mismatch notes — sometimes the KV "cash" was evicted too aggressively for canary traffic, that's on us to fix.

[02:00] Priya Singh: On Dedicated — we've onboarded two new Dedicated customers this quarter and increased baseline utilization. The Dedicated autoscaler now supports burst pools, but a reminder: burst policies need explicit config in the cluster YAML, we will add a UI toggle in the Console in the next sprint. Also, Private deployments: one pilot is in SOC2-inflight, their security review highlighted the need for KMS/HSM integration docs — we'll post that to the security repo.

[03:05] Samira Patel: Quick reliability note: we had two incidents in May, one was a networking regression tied to an underlying cloud driver, the other was an orchestration race when evicting KV caches during scale-down. Both are mitigations in place; postmortem for the cloud driver incident is up on confluence. We're increasing SLO error budget alerts so on-call sees these earlier.

[04:00] Diego Ramos: Ok product roadmap. We're prioritizing three pillars: 1) Performance & cost toolkit (Optimize), 2) Private & enterprise readiness (Private), and 3) Developer DX (console + SDKs). We're backfilling the model catalog with vetted quantized variants; expect 2 model additions this quarter. Also working on function/tool calling improvements and structured output for tool-augmented flows.

[04:45] Diego Ramos: On Optimize, the recommendation engine for batching and quant profiles will be in alpha next month. It's gonna be opinionated — e.g., "if p95 latency < 300ms and 90% of traffic <= 512 tokens then use profile A" — that'll be configurable. We're also adding a rollback button on rollouts to make canaries safer.

[05:30] Alex Morgan: A couple business notes — fundraising update: we're not actively raising right now; cash runway is healthy, but we will revisit later this year. Sales: Diego, Jae, big push on dedicated expansion into EU customers — need tighter legal playbooks for data residency.

[06:00] Jae Kim: Thanks. Customer update: we've closed a couple of POC-to-paid conversions, and renewals are looking good. A recurring ask from enterprise buyers is deeper compliance artifacts — beyond SOC2, they're asking for ISO docs and detailed network diagrams showing VPC peering options. We'll partner with security to standardize that deliverable.

[07:00] Audience question (Q: How will pricing change with Optimize?):
[07:15] Diego Ramos: Short answer — no headline changes yet. Optimize introduces suggested config that can reduce unit costs; pricing will stay usage-based but we will publish a FAQ and some example bill-of-materials showing cost impact. Sales to circulate soon.

[08:00] Alex Morgan: On hiring — we've approved 18 new roles across eng, product, and sales for Q3. Priority hires are infra SREs and backend engineers focusing on batching/compilation, and an enterprise security PM to help with compliance pack delivery. People Ops will post job descriptions and interview rubrics.

[09:00] Priya Singh: Technical note on kernels: the selector is heuristics + telemetry. We saw an edge case where longer sequences picked a kernel optimized for short kernels due to a sampling bug. That's patched, but it shows we need better unit tests and more synthetic scenarios in CI.

[10:00] Samira Patel: Also rolling out a canary workflow for infra changes — smaller batches, region-based, and an automated rollback trigger if latency or error rate crosses thresholds. We're hoping to avoid the scale-down race conditions that bit us last month.

[11:00] Audience question about Private/on-prem options latency and support:
[11:20] Priya Singh: Private setups vary a lot. For on-prem installs we've seen network throughput and NVLink topology cause variable KV cache performance. We'll publish a vendor guidance doc — recommended NICs, tuning knobs, and expected perf ranges. Support model: enterprise tier gets 24/7 pager coverage, Private deployments also qualify for on-site accomps if required.

[12:30] Alex Morgan: A small policy update — we are standardizing release notes cadence. Every Friday we'll publish an ops digest: deploys, incidents, perf regressions, and mitigation steps. It's to improve cross-team visibility.

[13:00] Diego Ramos: Product spotlight: we're demoing a new "route by policy" feature that lets you set rules to route by latency targets, geography, or cost. It's still in beta, but early customers show 7-15% cost improvements for mixed workloads. We'll run a wider beta soon.

[14:15] Audience interruption / cross-talk: someone says "that's huge" / laughs / "will it support model variant fallback?"
[14:30] Diego Ramos: Yes, model variant fallback is builtin — you can specify compatible fallback chains. There's ongoing work to make the compatibility matrix more explicit in the Console.

[15:00] Jae Kim: Customer success is building a renewal playbook for Dedicated accounts — focusing on throughput SLOs, cost optimization reviews, and a quarterly business review template. If your AE/CS team needs templates ping Jae.

[16:00] Alex Morgan: Open Q&A — please raise your hand or drop in chat.

[16:20] Employee (Q): Any update on open source contributions / community models?

[16:30] Priya Singh: We're continuing with model vetting and some contributions to the runtime optimizations upstream. The kernel work will likely be contributed as small patches where licensing allows. We also will host a community benchmark next quarter.

[17:10] Employee (Q): Hiring and leveling question: how do we decide IC vs manager roles for the new hires?

[17:25] People Ops: We'll share the role rubric, and managers should partner with People Ops on leveling. If there are internal promos, team leads should nominate by end of June.

[18:00] Samira Patel: Reliability hiring: two SREs and one senior infra eng in pipeline, please prioritize interviews for candidates with experience in orchestration and GPU infra — e.g., k8s custom schedulers or similar.

[19:00] Audience Q: Are we changing pricing for Hosted tenants because of the improved batching?

[19:10] Alex Morgan: No immediate pricing change. We view batching/Optimize as a product that lowers customers' unit costs through better config; we'll present case studies first. Any change that affects revenue will go through leadership and we'll communicate transparently.

[20:00] Diego Ramos: Quick demo note — function calling and structured output is getting more robust. We're adding deterministic output validation steps to reduce hallucinations in tool calls. Expect a small beta next sprint.

[21:00] Jae Kim: Customer highlight: A large fintech customer moved from POC to Dedicated after our dedicated latency profile matched their throughput SLA. They asked for stronger audit logs and a longer log retention window; security is working on retention options.

[22:00] Alex Morgan: OK, short shoutouts — hiring, infra, product — huge work. Also a thank you to CS for closing those renewals.

[22:30] Audience Q: Roadmap prioritization — when will we decide the next big feature?

[22:40] Diego Ramos: Priorities are set by OKRs; we meet weekly with PMs + Eng leads and will publish a more detailed roadmap by 6/18. Input welcome via the product channel.

[23:20] Alex Morgan: Final notes: please review the new code of conduct update and complete the training by end of month. We will have a town hall for UK/EU timezone friendly times next week.

[23:50] Priya Singh: I will share the infra perf spreadsheet and the kernel selector notes after this call: link in #infra. Also will attach a brief runbook for Private installs.

[24:10] Samira Patel: I'll follow up with the incident postmortem link and the reliability plan — expect action items assigned in the doc.

[24:30] Jae Kim: I'll share the renewal playbook and the Customer win deck.

[24:50] Alex Morgan: Great. Thanks all. Meeting adjourned.

Note: transcription contains occasional mis-hearings ("KV cash" -> KV cache, "Dedic8" -> Dedicated). Links referenced in call: infra perf spreadsheet (internal link), SOC2 compliance pack (internal link), roadmap doc (internal link).
